object_types.name: Customer
object_types.definition: A person or organization that places orders; identified by a unique customer ID in the CRM system.

source_references.excerpt: A customer places an order.
Each customer has a unique customer ID in the CRM system.

object_types.name: CustomerId
object_types.definition: Unique identifier for a customer in the CRM system.

source_references.excerpt: Each customer has a unique customer ID in the CRM system.

object_types.name: CustomerName
object_types.definition: The name of a customer, tracked as a text field.

source_references.excerpt: Yes, every customer has a name. It's just a text field.

object_types.name: Order
object_types.definition: A purchase order placed by a customer; identified by an order number.

source_references.excerpt: A customer places an order.
Each order has an order number. That's the primary identifier.

object_types.name: OrderNumber
object_types.definition: The primary identifier for an order.

source_references.excerpt: Each order has an order number. That's the primary identifier.

object_types.name: Product
object_types.definition: An item that can be included in orders; identified by SKU.

source_references.excerpt: An order contains one or more products.
By SKU -- a unique stock-keeping unit code.

object_types.name: Sku
object_types.definition: A unique stock-keeping unit code identifying a product.

source_references.excerpt: By SKU -- a unique stock-keeping unit code.

object_types.name: Quantity
object_types.definition: The quantity of a product specified on an order line.

source_references.excerpt: Each line in the order specifies a product and a quantity.

object_types.name: OrderStatus
object_types.definition: The status of an order, restricted to a fixed set of values.

source_references.excerpt: Yes, an order has a status. The possible values are: pending, confirmed, shipped, and delivered.

ambiguities.description: The billing team's 'client' term applies only to customers who have actually paid, which is a narrower concept than 'customer.' Is 'Client' truly a synonym for 'Customer', or does it represent a subtype/state (e.g., 'Paying Customer') that should be modeled separately with its own constraints?

source_references.excerpt: In our CRM they're "customers" but the billing team calls them "clients." For our purposes they're the same concept but the billing team has a slightly different definition -- they only consider someone a client once they've actually paid.

ambiguities.description: Order status is described as a simple current value. Is order status history tracked (e.g., timestamps for when an order transitioned to 'shipped' or 'delivered'), or is only the current status stored?

source_references.excerpt: Yes, an order has a status. The possible values are: pending, confirmed, shipped, and delivered.

ambiguities.description: Quantity per order line is captured, but it's unclear whether a product can appear on multiple distinct lines within the same order (e.g., different batches) or whether the order-product pair is strictly unique per order, which affects the uniqueness constraint on the ternary fact type.
